record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.context_brief: EFT versus traditional higher-order QED corrections
record.original_question: What is the exact correspondence between effective-field-theory treatments of higher-order QED effects and traditional finite-Z beta-decay radiative-correction calculations? The comparison should resolve discrepancies in two-loop anomalous dimensions, large-logarithm resummation, the Coulomb/Fermi-function treatment, and finite order-alpha-squared-Z terms for both neutron decay and nuclear beta decays with finite daughter charge Z.

evidence.quote: Recently, however, this methodology is under scrutiny, as approaches using effective field theory find different results and stress the need for proper matching between scales in consistent renormalization schemes. Specifically, the differences appear in the large-log summation and the treatment of the Fermi function
differences at the two-loop anomalous dimensions remain for both LEFT to HBChPT and HBChPT to me RGE’s, but introduce O(0.01%) corrections to ∆R which almost completely cancel.
The exact correspondence for the neutron as well as for finite Z needs to be further investigated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider beta decay (neutron decay and nuclear beta decay with a daughter nucleus of finite charge Z) and its higher-order QED radiative corrections to the differential and total decay rates. Two computational frameworks exist:

(A) The traditional finite-Z radiative-correction program, in which the Coulomb interaction with the nucleus is resummed via the relativistic Fermi function F(Z,E), and short-distance/long-distance QED corrections are organized as an expansion in α with the inner correction ΔR computed at fixed orders in α and αZ, including order-α²Z terms.

(B) An effective-field-theory tower in which the Standard Model is matched onto LEFT (low-energy effective field theory) at the electroweak scale, then onto heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory (HBChPT), with renormalization-group evolution between scales used to resum large logarithms log(M_W/m_e), log(m_p/m_e), etc., and with the Fermi-function/Coulomb effects represented through matching coefficients and operator anomalous dimensions.

Provide the exact, scheme-independent correspondence between (A) and (B), specifically:

1. Identify the precise mapping between the operator anomalous dimensions in framework (B) (through two-loop order, both LEFT → HBChPT and HBChPT → QED RGEs) and the corresponding terms in the traditional fixed-order calculation of ΔR in framework (A).

2. Reconcile the differing prescriptions for large-logarithm resummation between the two frameworks.

3. Establish the matching of the Fermi/Coulomb function F(Z,E) of framework (A) onto the EFT operator basis and Wilson coefficients of framework (B), valid for both Z = 1 (neutron decay) and finite daughter charge Z relevant to superallowed nuclear beta decays.

4. Account for all finite α²Z terms, demonstrating their equivalence (or computing the residual scheme-dependent differences) in the two frameworks.

The goal is a complete dictionary, valid for arbitrary Z, that explains the observed numerical discrepancies between EFT-based and traditional evaluations of ΔR (currently appearing at the level of O(0.01%) in the two-loop anomalous-dimension contribution).
artifact.category_tag: Effective field theory radiative corrections in beta decay
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has formulated the Fermi function as a field-theory matrix element and provided a factorization formula with operator anomalous dimensions through three loops, computing new α-order coefficients and demonstrating that EFT and nonrelativistic-Fermi-function results begin to differ at two-loop order. Subsequent papers (2024–2025) have extended factorization and resummation to neutron beta decay and superallowed decays in EFT. However, a complete, fully reconciled dictionary covering all finite-Z α²Z terms, large-log resummation, and Fermi-function matching for both neutron decay and arbitrary daughter charge Z is still under active development; thus the problem appears partially solved rather than fully closed.

status_evidence.title: Field Theory of the Fermi Function
status_evidence.snippet: Formulates the Fermi function as a field-theoretic object with anomalous dimension through three loops; results differ from the nonrelativistic Fermi-function ansatz at two-loop order.
status_evidence.claim: EFT recasting of Fermi function is now available; discrepancy with traditional treatment begins at two loops.

status_evidence.title: The Fermi function and the neutron's lifetime
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses how the Fermi-function enhancement for neutron decay is governed by the universal cusp anomalous dimension and is justified only at large Z in traditional treatments.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-Z correspondence is being clarified but not yet fully unified for arbitrary Z.

status_evidence.title: Factorization and resummation of QED radiative corrections for neutron beta decay
status_evidence.snippet: Provides EFT factorization and large-log resummation specifically for neutron beta decay.
status_evidence.claim: Neutron-specific EFT/traditional comparison continues to be developed in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Radiative Corrections to Superallowed β Decays in Effective Field Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Extends EFT-based radiative corrections to nuclear superallowed decays with finite Z.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-Z EFT calculation extended to superallowed transitions, addressing part of the dictionary.
